description: Structuring software at the class and system level: design principles such as SOLID, coupling and cohesion, the creational, structural and behavioural design patterns, architectural styles from layered to event-driven and microservices, quality attributes and their trade-offs, and documenting and evaluating architecture. Every pattern is implemented, refactored into and tested in the browser code lab, and every style is exercised on a running system whose behaviour under load and failure students can observe.
modelledOn: Gamma, Helm, Johnson and Vlissides, Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software
Bass, Clements and Kazman, Software Architecture in Practice
outcomes: Apply SOLID and related design principles to reduce coupling, increase cohesion and refactor code smells.
Select, implement and justify creational, structural and behavioural design patterns for a given design problem.
Compare architectural styles and choose one, or a combination, that fits a system's requirements and constraints.
Analyse quality attributes with scenarios and apply architectural tactics to meet them, explaining the trade-offs.
Document an architecture with multiple views and decision records and evaluate it with a structured method.

units.title: Design principles: SOLID, coupling and cohesion
topics: Modularity, information hiding and abstraction; kinds of coupling and cohesion
SOLID: single responsibility, open-closed, Liskov substitution, interface segregation and dependency inversion
Composition over inheritance; the law of Demeter; DRY and YAGNI
UML class and sequence diagrams as design notation
Code smells and refactoring; refactoring towards patterns

units.title: Creational patterns
topics: Factory method and abstract factory
Builder and prototype
Singleton and why it is often an anti-pattern; testability concerns
Dependency injection and inversion-of-control containers
Object pools and lazy initialisation

units.title: Structural patterns
topics: Adapter: wrapping several mobile money provider APIs behind one payment interface
Facade and proxy: simplifying subsystems; remote, caching and protection proxies
Decorator: adding logging, retries and caching without subclassing
Composite and bridge
Flyweight and memory-conscious design for low-end devices
Comparing similar patterns: adapter, decorator, proxy and facade

units.title: Behavioural patterns
topics: Strategy and template method: pluggable fare-calculation rules for tro-tro routes
Observer and publish-subscribe; event handling in user interfaces
Command, memento and undo; chain of responsibility
State: modelling a transaction life cycle as a state machine
Iterator, mediator and visitor; interpreter in brief
Anti-patterns and pattern overuse

units.title: Architectural styles: layered, event-driven, microservices
topics: What architecture is: structures, views, components and connectors
Layered, client-server and pipe-and-filter styles; MVC and MVVM
Hexagonal (ports and adapters) and clean architecture
Event-driven architecture: message brokers, event sourcing and CQRS
Microservices versus the modular monolith; service boundaries and domain-driven design
Serverless and peer-to-peer styles in brief

units.title: Quality attributes and trade-offs
topics: Quality attribute scenarios: source, stimulus, environment, response and response measure
Tactics for availability, performance and scalability
Tactics for security, modifiability, testability and usability
Consistency and partition tolerance: the CAP theorem and eventual consistency
Designing for intermittent power and low bandwidth: offline queues, caching, retries and idempotent operations
Cost, time to market and team structure as architectural forces; Conway's law

units.title: Patterns for distributed systems
topics: API gateway, service discovery and backend-for-frontend
Resilience patterns: circuit breaker, bulkhead, timeout and retry with backoff
Data management: database per service, sagas and the outbox pattern
Migrating legacy systems with the strangler fig pattern

units.title: Documenting and evaluating architecture
topics: Views and viewpoints: the 4+1 view model and the C4 model
Architecture decision records and documenting rationale
Evaluation with ATAM: utility trees, sensitivity points and risks
Architecture fitness functions and conformance checking in code
Technical debt and architectural erosion
Capstone: design, document and evaluate the architecture for a city transport and fare-payment platform

schedule.title: Modularity and SOLID
schedule.exercise: Pick a class from any program you have written and list which SOLID principles it follows and breaks, with one improvement for each.

tasks.title: Draw a module diagram of a school fees system and mark the coupling between modules as low, medium or high, with a reason for each
Refactor a notification class that sends SMS, email and logs to separate classes that follow single responsibility and dependency inversion, and test them
Replace an inheritance hierarchy of seven report classes with composition, remove duplicated code and check that all old outputs still match

schedule.title: Design notation and refactoring
schedule.exercise: Read a 60-line code listing and list five code smells you can see with a suggested refactoring for each.

tasks.title: Draw a class diagram and a sequence diagram for a customer withdrawing cash from an agent, using correct notation for each
Find and remove four code smells in a given order-processing module using small refactorings, running the tests after each step
Refactor a long conditional-heavy function towards the Strategy pattern, proving with tests that behaviour is unchanged and a new case needs no edits

schedule.title: Creational patterns
schedule.exercise: Write a table listing each creational pattern, the problem it solves and a one-line example from a payments or transport application.

tasks.title: Implement a factory method that creates mobile money provider objects by name, and test it with three providers and one unknown name
Use the builder pattern to create a complex report configuration with optional fields, and compare the clarity with a constructor with ten arguments
Replace a singleton configuration class with dependency injection, then show how a test can supply a fake configuration without global state

schedule.title: Structural patterns I: adapter, facade, proxy, decorator
schedule.exercise: Explain with an example how a proxy and a decorator differ when both wrap an object with the same interface.

tasks.title: Wrap two incompatible mobile money APIs behind one payment interface using adapters and run the same checkout code against both
Add a caching proxy in front of a slow exchange-rate service, and show with a call counter that repeated lookups hit the cache
Stack logging, retry and caching decorators on a payment gateway client in different orders, and show how the order changes behaviour on failures

schedule.title: Structural patterns II: composite, bridge, flyweight
schedule.exercise: Compare the adapter, decorator, proxy and facade patterns in a table by intent, structure and when to prefer each.

tasks.title: Model a company organisation chart as a composite tree and draw the class diagram showing leaf and composite roles
Use the bridge pattern to separate message types from delivery channels, then add a new channel without touching message classes
Apply flyweight to a map with 50000 markers for a low-end phone, measure the memory saved against the naive version and state the trade-off

schedule.title: Behavioural patterns I
schedule.exercise: Write a short design note on how a ride fare calculator can change pricing rules without redeploying the application.

tasks.title: Implement pluggable fare rules for tro-tro routes with Strategy, adding a student discount rule and testing three journeys
Build an observer system where a ticket booking notifies SMS and dashboard subscribers, and show that unsubscribing stops updates
Add undo and redo to a text editor with command and memento, and validate it on a script of 15 edits

schedule.title: Behavioural patterns II and anti-patterns
schedule.exercise: Review a given piece of code that uses five patterns and say which ones are justified and which are over-engineering.

tasks.title: Draw the state diagram of a mobile money transaction from initiated to completed, failed or reversed, with the allowed transitions
Implement the transaction life cycle with the State pattern and prove illegal transitions are rejected in 10 test cases
Simplify an over-engineered module that uses visitors, mediators and a singleton for a simple task, and justify each pattern you remove

schedule.title: Architectural structures and styles
schedule.exercise: Describe the structure, components and connectors of an application you use daily and name the architectural style it most resembles.

tasks.title: Draw component and deployment views for a school portal and label each connector with the protocol or call type used
Redesign a monolithic ordering application as layered and then as MVC, and compare changes needed to add a new report in each
Convert a layered application into a hexagonal design with ports and adapters, and show how a database can be swapped without touching business rules

schedule.title: Event-driven, microservices and other styles
schedule.exercise: Write a half-page argument for starting a new startup product as a modular monolith rather than microservices.

tasks.title: Draw an event-driven design for order placement with a broker, publishers and subscribers, and trace one order across all components
Split a transport booking monolith into services with domain-driven boundaries, drawing the contexts and the data each one owns
Compare a modular monolith with a microservices design for a team of four developers on cost, deployment and failure handling, and recommend one

schedule.title: Quality attributes and tactics
schedule.exercise: Write two quality attribute scenarios for a fare payment platform, one for performance and one for availability, with measurable response measures.

tasks.title: Write a complete quality attribute scenario with source, stimulus, environment, response and response measure for a payment peak at month end
Choose three tactics to keep a ticketing platform available during peak load and mark where each fits on the architecture diagram
Evaluate competing designs against security, modifiability and testability scenarios in a case, and justify the trade-off you accept

schedule.title: Distributed trade-offs and constraints
schedule.exercise: Explain with an example why a payment system on poor connectivity may choose eventual consistency, and what it must do to stay safe.

tasks.title: Simulate two replicas with a network partition, show a conflicting write and implement a simple reconciliation rule
Build an offline queue with retries, backoff and idempotent operations, and show that a duplicated payment request is applied once
Balance cost, time to market and team structure in a case study of a start-up architecture, applying Conway's law to the proposed split

schedule.title: Integration and resilience patterns
schedule.exercise: Describe how a circuit breaker stops one failing service from taking the whole system down, with a short timeline.

tasks.title: Place an API gateway and a backend-for-frontend for web and mobile clients on a system diagram, and show routing for three requests
Implement timeout, retry with backoff and a circuit breaker around a flaky service call and show the state changes over 30 calls
Implement a saga with compensating actions across payment, inventory and delivery services, and show recovery when the delivery step fails

schedule.title: Documenting, evaluating and the capstone
schedule.exercise: Write one architecture decision record for a major choice in your capstone, covering context, options, decision and consequences.

tasks.title: Draw C4 context and container diagrams for a city fare-payment platform, and label the technology of each container
Run an architecture evaluation of a proposed design in a case by building a utility tree and identifying sensitivity points and risks
Design, document and evaluate the architecture for a city transport and fare-payment platform, with views, decision records and a risk register
